  last="${_bdb_hd_tok[${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}-1]}"
  case "$last" in '|'|'|&'|'&&'|'||') return 0 ;; esac
  return 1
}

# _bdb_hd_header <line> — parse one header line. Sets _hd_ops (heredoc count,
# -1 = unreadable), _hd_delim, _hd_quoted, _hd_tabs, _hd_cls, _hd_dests[],
# _hd_pipe (pipeline id of the heredoc on this line).
_bdb_hd_header() {
  local line="${1:-}" k nt t opi=-1 w seg=0 pipe=0
  local -a tpipe mtoks
  _hd_ops=0 _hd_delim="" _hd_quoted=0 _hd_tabs=0 _hd_cls=none _hd_pipe=-1
  _hd_dests=()
  if ! _bdb_hd_tokenize "$line"; then _hd_ops=-1; return; fi
  nt=${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}
  tpipe=()
  for ((k = 0; k < nt; k++)); do
    t="${_bdb_hd_tok[k]}"
    case "$t" in
      ';'|';;'|'&'|'&&'|'||'|'('|')') pipe=$((pipe + 1)); tpipe[k]=-1; continue ;;
      '|'|'|&') tpipe[k]=-1; continue ;;
    esac
    tpipe[k]=$pipe
    if [[ "$t" =~ ^[0-9]*'<<'-?$ ]]; then _hd_ops=$((_hd_ops + 1)); opi=$k; fi
  done
  (( _hd_ops == 1 )) || return
  w="${_bdb_hd_tok[opi+1]:-}"
  [[ "${_bdb_hd_tok[opi]}" == *'<<-' ]] && _hd_tabs=1
  if [[ "$w" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_dsq || "$w" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_ddq || "$w" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_dbs ]]; then
    _hd_delim="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"; _hd_quoted=1
  elif [[ "$w" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_dw ]]; then
    _hd_delim="$w"
  else
    _hd_ops=-1; return        # variable-expanded, mixed or missing delimiter
  fi
  _hd_pipe="${tpipe[opi]}"
  if _bdb_hd_ctx_bad "$line"; then _hd_cls=interpreter; return; fi
  _bdb_hd_tokenize "$line"    # _bdb_hd_ctx_bad reused the token buffer
  # Classify every member of the heredoc's pipeline; the most executing wins.
  local cls=nonexec
  k=0
  while (( k < nt )); do
    if [[ "${tpipe[k]}" != "$_hd_pipe" ]]; then k=$((k + 1)); continue; fi
    mtoks=()
    while (( k < nt )) && [[ "${tpipe[k]}" == "$_hd_pipe" ]]; do mtoks[${#mtoks[@]}]="${_bdb_hd_tok[k]}"; k=$((k + 1)); done
    _bdb_hd_member "${mtoks[@]}"
    case "$_hd_mcls" in
      interpreter) cls=interpreter ;;
      none) [[ "$cls" == interpreter ]] || cls=none ;;
    esac
    k=$((k + 1))
  done
  _hd_cls="$cls"
}

# _bdb_hd_segword <segment> → _hd_w (command word after wrapper stripping,
# quotes and an absolute path removed) and _hd_rest (the text after it).
_bdb_hd_segword() {
  local s="${1:-}" w guard=0
  _hd_w="" _hd_rest=""
  while (( guard < 64 )); do
    guard=$((guard + 1))
    s="${s#"${s%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
    [[ -n "$s" ]] || return
    case "${s:0:1}" in
      '('|'{'|'!'|'\'|'"'|"'") s="${s:1}"; continue ;;
    esac
    w="${s%%[[:space:]]*}"
    s="${s:${#w}}"
    if [[ "$w" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_assign ]]; then continue; fi
    case "$w" in
      sudo|doas|command|exec|env|nice|time|nohup|builtin|stdbuf|ionice)
        while :; do
          s="${s#"${s%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
          case "$s" in
            -S|-S[[:space:]]*|--split-string*) _hd_w="sh"; _hd_rest="$s"; return ;;
            -[ugnCphUrtTDc]|-[ugnCphUrtTDc][[:space:]]*)
              s="${s:2}"; s="${s#"${s%%[![:space:]]*}"}"; w="${s%%[[:space:]]*}"; s="${s:${#w}}" ;;
            -*) w="${s%%[[:space:]]*}"; s="${s:${#w}}" ;;
            *) break ;;
          esac
        done
        continue ;;
    esac
    w="${w%%[\"\']*}"
    [[ "$w" == */* && "$w" != '$'* ]] && w="${w##*/}"
    _hd_w="$w"; _hd_rest="$s"
    return
  done
}

# _bdb_hd_scan_body <first> <last> <quoted> — per-segment scan of
# _bdb_hd_L[first..last]. Sets _hd_kept (fence-verb segments, one per line),
# _hd_synth (variable-command segments rewritten as rm/git/kubectl) and
# _hd_full (1 = the body needs the full scan).
_bdb_hd_scan_body() {
  local k l t seg
  _hd_kept="" _hd_synth="" _hd_full=0
  for ((k = $1; k <= $2; k++)); do
    l="${_bdb_hd_L[k]}"
    [[ "$l" == *'<<'* ]] && _hd_full=1
    if (( ! $3 )); then
      case "$l" in *'$('*|*'`'*|*'<('*|*'>('*) _hd_full=1 ;; esac
    fi
    t="${l//'&&'/$'\n'}"; t="${t//'||'/$'\n'}"; t="${t//'|'/$'\n'}"; t="${t//';'/$'\n'}"; t="${t//'&'/$'\n'}"
    while :; do
      seg="${t%%$'\n'*}"
      _bdb_hd_segword "$seg"
      if [[ -n "$_hd_w" ]]; then
        if [[ "$_hd_w" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_varw ]]; then
          _hd_full=1
          _hd_synth="${_hd_synth}rm${_hd_rest}"$'\n'"git${_hd_rest}"$'\n'"kubectl${_hd_rest}"$'\n'
        elif _bdb_hd_is_destructive "$_hd_w"; then
          _hd_kept="${_hd_kept}${_hd_w}${_hd_rest}"$'\n'
        elif _bdb_hd_is_interp "$_hd_w" || _bdb_hd_is_runner "$_hd_w"; then
          _hd_full=1
        fi
      fi
      [[ "$t" == *$'\n'* ]] || break
      t="${t#*$'\n'}"
    done
  done
}

# _bdb_hd_same_line_exec <basename> <header idx> <body first> <body last>
# → 0 when the target is named anywhere else in the command outside a safe
# reader (it may be executed, sourced, made executable, copied or moved).
_bdb_hd_same_line_exec() {
  local b="$1" hi="$2" bf="$3" bl="$4" k nt t u c cw seg_has pipe start j own
  for ((k = 0; k < _bdb_hd_n; k++)); do
    (( k >= bf && k <= bl )) && continue
    [[ "${_bdb_hd_L[k]}" == *"$b"* ]] || continue
    _bdb_hd_tokenize "${_bdb_hd_L[k]}" || return 0
    nt=${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}
    start=0 pipe=0
    for ((j = 0; j <= nt; j++)); do
      t="${_bdb_hd_tok[j]:-}"
      if (( j < nt )) && ! [[ "$t" =~ ^(';'|';;'|'&'|'&&'|'||'|'('|')'|'|'|'|&')$ ]]; then continue; fi
      # segment [start, j)
      own=0
      (( k == hi && pipe == _hd_pipe_saved )) && own=1
      if (( ! own )); then
        seg_has=0 cw=""
        for ((c = start; c < j; c++)); do
          u="${_bdb_hd_tok[c]}"; u="${u//[\"\']/}"; u="${u##*/}"
          [[ "$u" == "$b" ]] && seg_has=1
        done
        if (( seg_has )); then
          _bdb_hd_segword "${_bdb_hd_tok[*]:start:j-start}"
          cw="$_hd_w"
          if ! _bdb_hd_is_safe_reader "$cw" || [[ "$cw" == "$b" ]]; then return 0; fi
        fi
      fi
      case "$t" in '|'|'|&') ;; *) pipe=$((pipe + 1)) ;; esac
      start=$((j + 1))
    done
  done
  return 1
}

# _bdb_heredoc_scrub <command> — print the scrub copy (non-executing heredoc
# bodies reduced to their fence-verb segments) and set _bdb_hd_class to the
# most executing class seen (interpreter > none > nonexec; none if no heredoc).
_bdb_heredoc_scrub() {
  local text="${1:-}" out="" i j found l cls ctx=0 seen="" d first
  _bdb_hd_class=none
  text="${text//$'\r\n'/$'\n'}"
  if [[ "$text" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_ctl ]]; then _bdb_hd_class=interpreter; printf '%s' "${1:-}"; return; fi
  text="${text%$'\n'}"
  _bdb_hd_L=()
  while IFS= read -r l; do _bdb_hd_L[${#_bdb_hd_L[@]}]="$l"; done <<< "$text"
  _bdb_hd_n=${#_bdb_hd_L[@]}
  i=0
  while (( i < _bdb_hd_n )); do
    l="${_bdb_hd_L[i]}"
    if [[ "$l" != *'<<'* ]]; then
      out="$out$l"$'\n'
      (( ctx )) || ! _bdb_hd_ctx_bad "$l" || ctx=1
      i=$((i + 1)); continue
    fi
    _bdb_hd_header "$l"
    if (( _hd_ops == 0 )); then
      out="$out$l"$'\n'
      (( ctx )) || ! _bdb_hd_ctx_bad "$l" || ctx=1
      i=$((i + 1)); continue
    fi
    if (( _hd_ops != 1 )); then _bdb_hd_class=interpreter; printf '%s' "${1:-}"; return; fi
    found=-1
    for ((j = i + 1; j < _bdb_hd_n; j++)); do
      d="${_bdb_hd_L[j]}"
      if (( _hd_tabs )); then while [[ "$d" == $'\t'* ]]; do d="${d#$'\t'}"; done; fi
      if [[ "$d" == "$_hd_delim" ]]; then found=$j; break; fi
    done
    if (( found < 0 )); then _bdb_hd_class=interpreter; printf '%s' "${1:-}"; return; fi
    cls="$_hd_cls"
    (( ctx )) && cls=interpreter
    _hd_pipe_saved="$_hd_pipe"
    if [[ "$cls" == nonexec ]]; then
      first="${_bdb_hd_L[i+1]:-}"
      (( i + 1 < found )) || first=""
      first="${first#"${first%%[![:blank:]]*}"}"
      [[ "$first" == '#!'* ]] && cls=interpreter
    fi
    if [[ "$cls" == nonexec ]]; then
      local -a dests
      dests=(${_hd_dests[@]+"${_hd_dests[@]}"})
      for d in ${dests[@]+"${dests[@]}"}; do
        if _bdb_hd_exec_dest "$d" || _bdb_hd_same_line_exec "${d##*/}" "$i" $((i + 1)) $((found - 1)); then
          cls=interpreter; break
        fi
      done
    fi
    _bdb_hd_scan_body $((i + 1)) $((found - 1)) "$_hd_quoted"
    out="$out$l"$'\n'
    if [[ "$cls" == nonexec ]] && (( ! _hd_full )); then
      # #1245 special case: a standalone quoted `cat <<'W' [> path]` drops it all.
      if ! (( i == 0 && found == _bdb_hd_n - 1 && _hd_quoted )) || ! _bdb_hd_plain_cat "$l"; then
        out="$out$_hd_kept"
      fi
    else
      [[ "$cls" == nonexec ]] && cls=interpreter
      for ((j = i + 1; j < found; j++)); do out="$out${_bdb_hd_L[j]}"$'\n'; done
      out="$out$_hd_synth"
    fi
    out="$out${_bdb_hd_L[found]}"$'\n'
    (( ctx )) || ! _bdb_hd_ctx_bad "$l" || ctx=1
    case "$cls" in
      interpreter) seen=interpreter ;;
      none) [[ "$seen" == interpreter ]] || seen=none ;;
      nonexec) [[ -n "$seen" ]] || seen=nonexec ;;
    esac
    i=$((found + 1))
  done
  _bdb_hd_class="${seen:-none}"
  printf '%s' "${out%$'\n'}"
}

# The #1245 header grammar (byte-identical to _bdb_scrub_cat_heredoc's).
_bdb_hd_plain_cat() {
  local header="${1:-}" marker candidate
  local delimiter_re="<<(-?)('([[:alnum:]_]+)'|\"([[:alnum:]_]+)\")"
  local path_re="([[:alnum:]_./-]+|'[[:alnum:]_ ./-]+'|\"[[:alnum:]_ ./-]+\")"
  local header_re="^[[:blank:]]*cat[[:blank:]]+(HEREDOC([[:blank:]]+>>?[[:blank:]]*${path_re})?|>>?[[:blank:]]*${path_re}[[:blank:]]+HEREDOC)[[:blank:]]*$"
  [[ "$header" =~ $delimiter_re ]] || return 1
  marker="${BASH_REMATCH[0]}"
  candidate="${header/"$marker"/HEREDOC}"
  [[ "$candidate" =~ $header_re ]]
}

# Knob: destructive_command_guard.heredoc_classifier in the repo's
# .loa.config.yaml (read once, no fork, only for commands holding `<<`).
# Only an explicit false|no|off turns it off; turning it off only tightens.
_bdb_heredoc_knob_on() {
  local cfg="${LOA_REPO_ROOT:-${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-.}}/.loa.config.yaml" content="" l in_blk=0
  [[ -f "$cfg" && -r "$cfg" ]] || return 0
  IFS= read -r -d '' content < "$cfg" || true
  [[ "$content" == *heredoc_classifier* ]] || return 0
  while IFS= read -r l; do
    case "$l" in
      destructive_command_guard:*) in_blk=1; continue ;;
      [A-Za-z_]*) in_blk=0; continue ;;
    esac
    if (( in_blk )) && [[ "$l" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_knob ]]; then
      case "${BASH_REMATCH[1]}" in false|False|FALSE|no|No|NO|off|Off|OFF) return 1 ;; esac
    fi
  done <<< "$content"
  return 0
}

# Exported entry points (source with BDB_LIB_ONLY=1).
_bdb_heredoc_consumer_class() {
  local LC_ALL=C
  _bdb_heredoc_scrub "${1:-}" >/dev/null

heredoc_nonexec() {
  [[ "$(_bdb_heredoc_consumer_class "${1:-}")" == nonexec ]]

   222	  vj=$(bash "$VERDICT_DERIVE" --file "$f" --gate "$g" --json 2>/dev/null) || true
   223	  jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1 <<<"$vj" || vj='{"trailer_found":false,"verdict":null,"counts":null,"exit_code":1}'
   224	  tl=$(grep -E '^<!-- LOA-VERDICT \{.*\} -->[[:space:]]*$' "$f" 2>/dev/null | tail -n 1) || tl=""
   225	  pj=$(printf '%s' "$tl" | sed -E 's/^<!-- LOA-VERDICT (.*) -->[[:space:]]*$/\1/')
   226	  jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1 <<<"$pj" || pj='{}'
   227	  if [[ "$(jq -r '.trailer_found' <<<"$vj")" == true ]]; then
   228	    hash=$(printf '%s\n' "$vj" | jq -Sc '{verdict,counts}' | _md5)
   229	  else
   230	    hash=$( { grep -A 100 "## Findings\|## Issues\|## Changes Required" "$f" 2>/dev/null || true; } | head -50 | _md5)
   231	  fi
   232	  jq -nc --arg f "$rel" --argjson v "$vj" --argjson p "$pj" --arg h "$hash" '
   233	    def sid: if type == "string" and test("^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}$") then . else null end;
   234	    def tsv: if type == "string" and test("^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9:.]+Z$") then . else null end;
   235	    {file: $f, exists: true, trailer: ($v.trailer_found == true),
   236	     verdict: ($v.verdict | if type == "string" then . else null end),
   237	     counts: ($v.counts // null), exit_code: ($v.exit_code // 1),
   238	     sprint_id: ($p.sprint_id | sid), ts: ($p.ts | tsv), hash: $h}
   239	    | .approved = (.exit_code == 0 and .verdict == "APPROVED")'
   240	}
   241	
   242	# impl_commit SINCE → "sha epoch" of the newest non-merge commit on HEAD since
   243	# SINCE touching a path outside the state/generated set, or nothing
   244	impl_commit() {
   245	  git -C "$root" rev-parse --git-dir >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
   246	  git -C "$root" log --no-merges -n 1 --format='%H %ct' ${1:+"--since=$1"} -- . \
   247	    ':(exclude,glob)grimoires/**' ':(exclude,glob).run/**' ':(exclude,glob)**/REPO-MAP.md' \
   248	    ':(exclude,glob)**/checksums.json' ':(exclude,glob)**/CHANGELOG.md' 2>/dev/null || true
   249	}
   250	
   251	# The ordered rounds of one sprint directory: every -rN file, then the current
   252	# file unless it is byte-identical to the highest -rN of its gate
   253	rounds_of() {
   254	  local dir="$1" g base f n top topn cur
   255	  for g in review audit; do
   256	    if [[ "$g" == review ]]; then base=engineer-feedback; else base=auditor-sprint-feedback; fi
   257	    top=""; topn=-1
   258	    for f in "$dir/$base"-r*.md; do
   259	      [[ -f "$f" ]] || continue
   260	      n=${f##*-r}; n=${n%.md}
   261	      [[ "$n" =~ ^[0-9]{1,6}$ ]] || continue
   262	      fb_parse "$f" "$g" | jq -c --arg g "$g" --argjson n "$((10#$n))" '. + {gate: $g, round: $n}'
   263	      if (( 10#$n > topn )); then topn=$((10#$n)); top="$f"; fi
   264	    done
   265	    cur="$dir/$base.md"
   266	    if [[ -f "$cur" ]] && ! { [[ -n "$top" ]] && cmp -s "$cur" "$top"; }; then
   267	      fb_parse "$cur" "$g" | jq -c --arg g "$g" '. + {gate: $g, round: 999999}'
   268	    fi
   269	  done
   270	}
   271	
   272	# Shared jq definitions: time, the breaker recompute and the run-state resolution
   273	JQ_DEFS='
   274	def epoch: if type == "string" then (sub("\\.[0-9]+Z$"; "Z") | try fromdateiso8601 catch null) else null end;
   275	def fresh($now; $win): epoch as $t | $t != null and ($now - $t) <= $win and ($t - $now) <= 300;
   276	def recompute($rounds; $reset):
   277	  ($rounds
   278	   | map(select($reset == null or ((.ts // "") > $reset)))
   279	   | sort_by([(.ts // ""), .round, (if .gate == "review" then 0 else 1 end)])
   280	   | map(select(.approved | not))) as $nr
   281	  | reduce $nr[] as $r ({cycle: 0, same: 0, hash: null, np: 0, lc: null};
   282	      .cycle += 1
   283	      | (if $r.hash != "none" and $r.hash == .hash then .same += 1 else .same = 1 | .hash = $r.hash end)
   284	      | ($r.counts | tojson) as $c
   285	      | (if .lc != null and .lc == $c then .np += 1 else .np = 0 end)
   286	      | .lc = $c);
   287	def skeleton($th; $ts):
   288	  {state: "CLOSED",
   289	   triggers: {same_issue: {count: 0, threshold: $th.same, last_hash: null},
   290	              no_progress: {count: 0, threshold: $th.np},
   291	              cycle_count: {current: 0, limit: $th.cycles},
   292	              timeout: {started: $ts, limit_hours: $th.hours}},
   293	   history: []};
   294	def merge_breaker($rc; $th; $ts):
   295	  (if type == "object" then . else skeleton($th; $ts) end)
   296	  | .triggers = (.triggers // {})
   297	  | .triggers.cycle_count.current = ([(.triggers.cycle_count.current // 0), $rc.cycle] | max)
   298	  | (if $rc.same > (.triggers.same_issue.count // 0)
   299	     then .triggers.same_issue.count = $rc.same | .triggers.same_issue.last_hash = $rc.hash else . end)
   300	  | (if $rc.np > (.triggers.no_progress.count // 0) or (.triggers.no_progress.last_counts == null and $rc.lc != null)
   301	     then .triggers.no_progress.count = ([(.triggers.no_progress.count // 0), $rc.np] | max)
   302	          | .triggers.no_progress.last_counts = $rc.lc else . end)
   303	  | ( if (.triggers.same_issue.count // 0) >= (.triggers.same_issue.threshold // $th.same)
   304	        then ["same_issue", "same issue hash repeated \(.triggers.same_issue.count) times (derived from the feedback history)"]
   305	      elif (.triggers.no_progress.count // 0) >= (.triggers.no_progress.threshold // $th.np)
   306	        then ["no_progress", "counts unchanged for \(.triggers.no_progress.count) consecutive rounds (derived from the feedback history)"]
   307	      elif (.triggers.cycle_count.current // 0) >= (.triggers.cycle_count.limit // $th.cycles)
   308	        then ["cycle_count", "\(.triggers.cycle_count.current) changes-required rounds (derived from the feedback history)"]
   309	      else null end ) as $trip
   310	  | if $trip != null and (.state // "CLOSED") != "OPEN"
   311	    then .state = "OPEN" | .history = ((.history // []) + [{timestamp: $ts, trigger: $trip[0], reason: $trip[1], source: "derive"}])
   312	    else .state = (.state // "CLOSED") end;
   313	def known_ids: (.derivation.sprint_ids // null) // ((.sprints.list // []) | map(.id? // empty));
   314	def resolve($f; $now; $win):
   315	  . as $c
   316	  | (if ($c | type) == "object" then $c else {} end) as $c
   317	  | ($c.state // $c.status // "") as $cs
   318	  | ($c | known_ids) as $known
   319	  | ([$f.sprints[] | select(.state != "complete")
   320	      | "sprint-\(.global_id)" as $g | .local_label as $l
   321	      | select(($known | index($g)) == null and ($l == "" or ($known | index($l)) == null))] | length > 0) as $new
   322	  | ((($c.completion // {}) | .merged_sha? // "") | type == "string" and length > 0) as $merged
   323	  | if ($c.state // "") == "JACKED_OUT" or ($c.status // "") == "JACKED_OUT" or $merged then "JACKED_OUT"
   324	    elif $f.breaker_open or $cs == "HALTED" then "HALTED"
   325	    elif $f.all_complete then "COMPLETE"
   326	    elif $cs == "COMPLETE" and ($new | not) then "COMPLETE"
   327	    elif ($c.timestamps.last_activity? // null) | fresh($now; $win) then "RUNNING"
   328	    else "INTERRUPTED" end;
   329	'
   330	
   331	cmd_derive() {
   332	  local ledger="$root/grimoires/loa/ledger.json" a2a="$root/grimoires/loa/a2a" active rows
   333	  if [[ ! -f "$ledger" ]] || ! jq -e 'type == "object"' "$ledger" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
   334	    echo "run-checkpoint: derive: no readable ledger at $ledger — callers keep the cache" >&2; return 4
   335	  fi
   336	  active=$(jq -r '.active_cycle // empty | strings' "$ledger")
   337	  if [[ -z "$active" ]] || ! jq -e --arg c "$active" 'any(.cycles[]?; .id == $c)' "$ledger" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
   338	    echo "run-checkpoint: derive: the ledger has no active cycle — callers keep the cache" >&2; return 4
   339	  fi
   340	  local win now now_ts fa=1 th
   341	  win=$(( $(cfg_int '.run_mode.stale_hours' 12 8760) * 3600 ))
   342	  [[ "$(cfg '.run_mode.file_authoritative')" == false ]] && fa=0
   343	  th=$(jq -nc --argjson s "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.circuit_breaker.same_issue_threshold' 3 1000)" \
   344	              --argjson n "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.circuit_breaker.no_progress_threshold' 5 1000)" \
   345	              --argjson c "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.defaults.max_cycles' 20 10000)" \
   346	              --argjson h "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.defaults.timeout_hours' 8 8760)" \
   347	              '{same: $s, np: $n, cycles: $c, hours: $h}')
   348	  now=$(date +%s); now_ts=$(now_iso)
   349	
   350	  # Per-sprint facts
   351	  local sprints="[]" gid label lstatus since dir rv au mex msid ic sj
   352	  rows=$(jq -r --arg c "$active" '
   353	    (.cycles[] | select(.id == $c)) as $cy
   354	    | ($cy.sprints // [])[]
   355	    | select((.global_id | type) == "number")
   356	    | [(.global_id | tostring), ((.local_label // "") | tostring), ((.status // "") | tostring),
   357	       ([.started, .created, $cy.created] | map(select(type == "string" and test("^[0-9]{4}-")))
   358	        | if length == 0 then "" else ([.[0], ($cy.created // "")] | max) end)]
   359	    | map(if . == "" then "-" else . end)
   360	    | @tsv' "$ledger")
   361	  # "-" stands for an empty field: IFS whitespace (tab) would collapse two adjacent separators
   362	  while IFS=$'\t' read -r gid label lstatus since; do
   363	    [[ "$gid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || continue
   364	    [[ "$label" == - ]] && label=""
   365	    [[ "$since" == - ]] && since=""
   366	    [[ "$label" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}$ ]] || label=""
   367	    [[ "$lstatus" =~ ^[a-z_]{1,32}$ ]] || lstatus="unknown"
   368	    [[ "$since" =~ ^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9:.]+Z$ ]] || since=""
   369	    dir="$a2a/sprint-$gid"
   370	    rv=$(fb_parse "$dir/engineer-feedback.md" review)
   371	    au=$(fb_parse "$dir/auditor-sprint-feedback.md" audit)
   372	    mex=false; msid=""
   373	    if [[ -f "$dir/COMPLETED" ]]; then
   374	      mex=true
   375	      msid=$(sed -n 's/^sprint:[[:space:]]*\([A-Za-z0-9._-]*\).*/\1/p' "$dir/COMPLETED" | head -n 1) || msid=""
   376	    fi
   377	    ic=$(impl_commit "$since")
   378	    sj=$(jq -nc --argjson gid "$gid" --arg label "$label" --arg status "$lstatus" --argjson rv "$rv" --argjson au "$au" \
   379	              --argjson mex "$mex" --arg msid "$msid" --arg ic "$ic" '
   380	      def mine: type == "string" and length > 0 and (. == "sprint-\($gid)" or ($label != "" and . == $label));
   381	      ($rv.approved == true and ($rv.sprint_id | mine)) as $R
   382	      | ($au.approved == true and ($au.sprint_id | mine)) as $A
   383	      | ([$rv.sprint_id, $au.sprint_id, (if $msid == "" then null else $msid end)] | map(select(type == "string" and length > 0))) as $ids
   384	      | ($mex and any($ids[]; mine | not)) as $stale
   385	      | ($mex and ($stale | not) and (($rv.sprint_id | mine) or ($au.sprint_id | mine))) as $M
   386	      | ($ic | split(" ")) as $c
   387	      | ([$rv.ts, $au.ts] | map(select(. != null)) | max) as $vts
   388	      | def verdict($x): if $x.exists then {verdict: $x.verdict, sprint_id: $x.sprint_id, consistent: ($x.exit_code == 0), file: $x.file} else null end;
   389	      {global_id: $gid, local_label: $label, status: $status,
   390	       completed_marker: $M, marker_present: $mex, stale_marker: $stale,
   391	       review: verdict($rv), audit: verdict($au),
   392	       impl_commit: (if ($c | length) == 2 then $c[0] else null end),
   393	       commit_after_verdict: (if ($c | length) == 2 and $vts != null
   394	                              then (($c[1] | tonumber) > ($vts | sub("\\.[0-9]+Z$"; "Z") | try fromdateiso8601 catch 0)) else null end),
   395	       legacy_feedback: ([$rv, $au] | map(select(.exists and (.trailer | not)) | .file)),
   396	       state: (if $M and $R and $A and $status == "completed" then "complete"
   397	               elif ($M | not) and $R and $A then "awaiting_marker" else "in_progress" end)}')
   398	    sprints=$(jq -c --argjson s "$sj" '. + [$s]' <<<"$sprints")
   399	  done <<<"$rows"
   400	
   401	  # Breaker recompute over the active sprint's ordered rounds
   402	  local active_gid rounds cache="null" cache_ok=1 bcache="null" reset rc merged
   403	  active_gid=$(jq -r 'if length == 0 then "" else ((map(select(.state != "complete")) | .[0]) // .[-1]) | .global_id | tostring end' <<<"$sprints")
   404	  rounds="[]"
   405	  if [[ -n "$active_gid" && -d "$a2a/sprint-$active_gid" ]]; then
   406	    rounds=$(rounds_of "$a2a/sprint-$active_gid" | jq -sc '.')
   407	  fi
   408	  if [[ -f "$file" ]]; then
   409	    if cache=$(jq -c . "$file" 2>/dev/null) && [[ -n "$cache" ]]; then :; else cache="null"; cache_ok=0; fi
   410	  fi
   411	  if [[ -f "$breaker" ]]; then bcache=$(jq -c 'if type == "object" then . else null end' "$breaker" 2>/dev/null) || bcache="null"; [[ -n "$bcache" ]] || bcache="null"; fi
   412	  reset=$(jq -c '.reset_at? // null | if type == "string" then . else null end' <<<"$bcache")
   413	  rc=$(jq -nc --argjson r "$rounds" --argjson z "$reset" "$JQ_DEFS"' recompute($r; $z)')
   414	  merged=$(jq -c --argjson rc "$rc" --argjson th "$th" --arg ts "$now_ts" "$JQ_DEFS"' merge_breaker($rc; $th; $ts)' <<<"$bcache")
   415	
   416	  local facts report
   417	  facts=$(jq -nc --argjson s "$sprints" --argjson b "$merged" '
   418	    {sprints: $s,
   419	     all_complete: (($s | length) > 0 and all($s[]; .state == "complete")),
   420	     breaker_open: ($b.state == "OPEN"),
   421	     stale_markers: [$s[] | select(.stale_marker) | "sprint-\(.global_id)"],
   422	     legacy_feedback: [$s[] | .legacy_feedback[]],
   423	     sprint_ids: [$s[] | "sprint-\(.global_id)"]}')
   424	  report=$(jq -nc --argjson f "$facts" --argjson c "$cache" --argjson b "$merged" --argjson rc "$rc" \
   425	                  --argjson now "$now" --argjson win "$win" --arg ts "$now_ts" --arg cycle "$active" \
   426	                  --argjson fa "$fa" --argjson cache_ok "$cache_ok" --arg ag "$active_gid" "$JQ_DEFS"'
   427	    def st: if type == "string" then (if test("^[A-Z_]{1,32}$") then . else "INVALID" end) else null end;
   428	    ($c | resolve($f; $now; $win)) as $s
   429	    | ($c | if type == "object" then (.state | st) else null end) as $cs
   430	    | ($c | if type == "object" then (.status | st) else null end) as $cst
   431	    | {cycle: $cycle, derived_at: $ts, stale_hours: ($win / 3600), file_authoritative: ($fa == 1),
   432	       state: $s, cache_state: $cs, cache_status: $cst,
   433	       cache: (if $cache_ok == 0 then "unparseable" elif $c == null then "missing" else "present" end),
   434	       drift: ($c != null and ($cs != $s or ($cst != null and $cst != $s))),
   435	       notes: ([
   436	         (if $cs != null and $cst != null and $cs != $cst then "cache .state \($cs) and .status \($cst) disagree" else empty end),
   437	         (if $s == "JACKED_OUT" and ($f.all_complete | not) then "JACKED_OUT is terminal: files show incomplete sprints; the cache is kept" else empty end),
   438	         (if $s == "COMPLETE" and ($f.all_complete | not) then "COMPLETE kept: no new incomplete sprint in the ledger" else empty end),
   439	         ($f.sprints[] | select(.stale_marker) | "sprint-\(.global_id): COMPLETED marker names another sp

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# profile-lib.sh — `loa.profile` resolution (cycle-129 SDD D-9.1, §5.3;
     4	# DEC-0143, DEC-0152, DEC-0166).
     5	#
     6	# Sourced API (bash 3.2 safe; sets no shell options; every function returns 0
     7	# unless stated):
     8	#   loa_profile                     → lean | standard | full
     9	#   loa_profile_source              → explicit | default | invalid
    10	#   loa_knob <yq-path> <fallback>   → the effective value of one config key:
    11	#        the key set explicitly in the config (an explicit `false` counts —
    12	#        never `// default`, which reads false as absent), else the selected
    13	#        profile's value when the key is a profile key, else <fallback>.
    14	#        Returns 2 (printing the fallback) on a malformed path.
    15	#   loa_profile_overrides           → `key=value` lines, one per explicit
    16	#        profile key whose value differs from the selected profile's value
    17	#   loa_effective_json              → the resolved document (below)
    18	#
    19	# CLI: profile-lib.sh profile | source | knob <path> <fallback> | overrides | json
    20	#
    21	# Inputs (each has a test seam):
    22	#   config    LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE, else LOA_STATUS_CONFIG_FILE (honoured
    23	#             only under bats, like loa-status.sh), else <root>/.loa.config.yaml
    24	#   profiles  LOA_PROFILES_FILE, else <root>/.claude/data/profiles.yaml
    25	#   floor     LOA_PROFILE_FLOOR_FILE, else <root>/.claude/data/floor.yaml
    26	#   root      LOA_PROFILE_ROOT, else three directories above this file
    27	#
    28	# Cache: <root>/.run/effective-config.json (LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE overrides),
    29	# keyed on the paths and the mtime+size of the config, profiles.yaml and
    30	# floor.yaml: any edit to one of them rebuilds it on the next call, so it is
    31	# built once per session in practice. When the config is a seam (not the
    32	# repository's own file) and no cache seam is set, nothing is cached — a test
    33	# config never overwrites the repository's cache. The warm path is one stat
    34	# and one jq. The write is atomic (temp file + mv in the same directory).
    35	#
    36	# Safety: a profile key that names a floor key (floor.yaml `floor_keys`, `*`
    37	# matches one or more characters; an ancestor of a floor key also counts) is
    38	# ignored with a WARN — no profile can reach the floor. Key paths are checked
    39	# against ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+(\.[A-Za-z0-9_]+)*$ before they reach a yq expression.
    40	# Overrides and the requested profile name are control-stripped and cut.
    41	# =============================================================================
    42	
    43	_LOA_PL_SELF="${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"
    44	_LOA_PL_SELF_DIR="${_LOA_PL_SELF%/*}"
    45	[[ "$_LOA_PL_SELF_DIR" == "$_LOA_PL_SELF" ]] && _LOA_PL_SELF_DIR="."
    46	_LOA_PL_SELF_DIR="$(cd "$_LOA_PL_SELF_DIR" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)"
    47	_LOA_PL_JSON=""
    48	_LOA_PL_ID=""
    49	
    50	_loa_pl_paths() {
    51	  local root="${LOA_PROFILE_ROOT:-}"
    52	  if [[ -z "$root" ]]; then
    53	    root="$(cd "$_LOA_PL_SELF_DIR/../../.." 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)"
    54	  fi
    55	  _LOA_PL_ROOT="$root"
    56	  local default_cfg="$root/.loa.config.yaml" status_cfg=""
    57	  # LOA_STATUS_CONFIG_FILE is loa-status.sh's bats-gated seam; honour it the same way.
    58	  if [[ -n "${BATS_TEST_FILENAME:-}${BATS_VERSION:-}" ]]; then
    59	    status_cfg="${LOA_STATUS_CONFIG_FILE:-}"
    60	  fi
    61	  _LOA_PL_CFG="${LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE:-${status_cfg:-$default_cfg}}"
    62	  _LOA_PL_PROF="${LOA_PROFILES_FILE:-$root/.claude/data/profiles.yaml}"
    63	  _LOA_PL_FLOOR="${LOA_PROFILE_FLOOR_FILE:-$root/.claude/data/floor.yaml}"
    64	  if [[ -n "${LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE:-}" ]]; then
    65	    _LOA_PL_CACHE="$LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE"
    66	  elif [[ "$_LOA_PL_CFG" == "$default_cfg" ]]; then
    67	    _LOA_PL_CACHE="$root/.run/effective-config.json"
    68	  else
    69	    _LOA_PL_CACHE=""
    70	  fi
    71	}
    72	
    73	# The cache key: the three paths plus one stat line per existing file. An
    74	# empty stat output for an existing file (no usable stat) disables caching.
    75	_loa_pl_id() {
    76	  local st
    77	  st=$(stat -Lc '%n|%y|%s' -- "$_LOA_PL_CFG" "$_LOA_PL_PROF" "$_LOA_PL_FLOOR" 2>/dev/null) ||
    78	    st=$(stat -Lf '%N|%Fm|%z' -- "$_LOA_PL_CFG" "$_LOA_PL_PROF" "$_LOA_PL_FLOOR" 2>/dev/null) || true
    79	  if [[ -z "$st" ]] && [[ -e "$_LOA_PL_CFG" || -e "$_LOA_PL_PROF" ]]; then
    80	    _LOA_PL_CUR_ID=""
    81	    return 0
    82	  fi
    83	  _LOA_PL_CUR_ID="v1|$_LOA_PL_CFG|$_LOA_PL_PROF|$_LOA_PL_FLOOR|${st//$'\n'/;}"
    84	}
    85	
    86	_loa_pl_warn() { printf '[profile-lib] WARN: %s\n' "$*" >&2; }
    87	
    88	# Builds the resolved document from the three inputs into _LOA_PL_JSON.
    89	_loa_pl_build() {
    90	  local cfg='{}' prof='{}' floor='[]' out
    91	  if ! command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || ! command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    92	    _LOA_PL_JSON=""
    93	    return 1
    94	  fi
    95	  if [[ -f "$_LOA_PL_CFG" ]]; then
    96	    if ! cfg=$(yq -o=json '.' "$_LOA_PL_CFG" 2>/dev/null); then

   191	    j=$(jq -c --arg id "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" 'if .schema_version == 1 and .id == $id then . else empty end' \
   192	        "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" 2>/dev/null) || j=""

   194	      _LOA_PL_JSON="$j"
   195	      _LOA_PL_ID="$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID"
   196	      return 0
   197	    fi
   198	  fi
   199	  _loa_pl_build || return 1
   200	  _LOA_PL_ID="$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID"
   201	  _loa_pl_write_cache
   202	  return 0
   203	}
   204	
   205	# Live read of one explicit key (non-profile keys, or no resolution available).
   206	_loa_pl_live() {
   207	  local key="$1" fallback="$2" v
   208	  if [[ -f "${_LOA_PL_CFG:-}" ]] && command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 && command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then

   211	      printf '%s\n' "$v"
   212	      return 0
   213	    fi
   214	  fi
   215	  printf '%s\n' "$fallback"
   216	  return 0
   217	}
   218	
   219	loa_knob() {
   220	  local path="${1:-}" fallback="${2:-}" key v
   221	  key="${path#.}"
   222	  if [[ ! "$key" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+(\.[A-Za-z0-9_]+)*$ ]]; then
   223	    _loa_pl_warn "loa_knob: malformed key path '${path//[^A-Za-z0-9._-]/?}'"
   224	    printf '%s\n' "$fallback"
   225	    return 2
   226	  fi
   227	  # Warm path: one stat + one jq straight from the cache file.
   228	  _loa_pl_paths
   229	  _loa_pl_id

   231	     command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
   232	    v=$(jq -r --arg id "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" --arg k "$key" '
   233	          if .schema_version == 1 and .id == $id then
   234	            (if (.knobs | has($k)) then .knobs[$k].value
   235	               | (if type == "string" then . elif type == "object" or type == "array" then tojson else tostring end)
   236	             else "__LOA_PL_MISS__" end)
   237	          else "__LOA_PL_STALE__" end' "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" 2>/dev/null) || v="__LOA_PL_STALE__"
   238	    if [[ "$v" == "__LOA_PL_MISS__" ]]; then
   239	      _loa_pl_live "$key" "$fallback"
   240	      return 0
   241	    fi
   242	    if [[ -n "$v" && "$v" != "__LOA_PL_STALE__" ]]; then
   243	      printf '%s\n' "$v"
   244	      return 0
   245	    fi
   246	  fi
   247	  if ! _loa_pl_load; then
   248	    _loa_pl_live "$key" "$fallback"
   249	    return 0
   250	  fi
   251	  v=$(printf '%s' "$_LOA_PL_JSON" | jq -r --arg k "$key" '
   252	        if (.knobs | has($k)) then .knobs[$k].value
   253	          | (if type == "string" then . elif type == "object" or type == "array" then tojson else tostring end)
   254	        else "__LOA_PL_MISS__" end' 2>/dev/null) || v="__LOA_PL_MISS__"
   255	  if [[ -z "$v" || "$v" == "__LOA_PL_MISS__" ]]; then
   256	    _loa_pl_live "$key" "$fallback"
   257	    return 0
   258	  fi
   259	  printf '%s\n' "$v"
   260	  return 0
   261	}
   262	
   263	loa_profile() {
   264	  if _loa_pl_load; then
   265	    printf '%s' "$_LOA_PL_JSON" | jq -r '.profile // "standard"' 2>/dev/null || echo standard
   266	  else
   267	    echo standard
   268	  fi
   269	  return 0
   270	}
   271	
   272	loa_profile_source() {
   273	  if _loa_pl_load; then
   274	    printf '%s' "$_LOA_PL_JSON" | jq -r '.profile_source // "default"' 2>/dev/null || echo default
   275	  else
   276	    echo default
   277	  fi
   278	  return 0
   279	}
   280	
   281	loa_profile_overrides() {
   282	  if _loa_pl_load; then
   283	    printf '%s' "$_LOA_PL_JSON" | jq -r '.overrides[]?' 2>/dev/null || true
   284	  fi
   285	  return 0
   286	}
   287	
   288	loa_effective_json() {
   289	  if _loa_pl_load; then
   290	    printf '%s\n' "$_LOA_PL_JSON"
   291	  else
   292	    echo '{}'
   293	  fi
   294	  return 0
   295	}
   296	
   297	if [[ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" == "${0}" ]]; then
   298	  export LC_ALL=C
   299	  case "${1:-}" in
   300	    profile)   loa_profile ;;
   301	    source)    loa_profile_source ;;
   302	    knob)      [[ $# -ge 2 ]] || { echo "usage: profile-lib.sh knob <yq-path> [fallback]" >&2; exit 2; }
   303	               loa_knob "$2" "${3:-}"; exit $? ;;
   304	    overrides) loa_profile_overrides ;;
   305	    json)      loa_effective_json ;;
   306	    *)         sed -n '3,/^# =====/p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//' >&2; exit 2 ;;
   307	  esac
   308	fi

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh — Karpathy principle 3 (Surgical Changes),
     3	# per-task diff size (#961 K-1 / FR-1; reworked by cycle-129 D-4.3, D-4.2a,
     4	# DEC-0141).
     5	#
     6	# PostToolUse:Write|Edit|NotebookEdit hook. Counts the lines each write adds
     7	# (Write → content, Edit/NotebookEdit → new_string) and keeps a running total
     8	# PER TASK:
     9	#
    10	#   key      the current task from `run-checkpoint.sh read --json`
    11	#            (`.checkpoint.task`, else the sprint), else the session id from
    12	#            the hook payload (`.session_id`, else LOA_SESSION_ID, else
    13	#            <user>-<UTC date>); sanitised to ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ (any other
    14	#            byte becomes `_`, a leading dot becomes `_`, cut to 128 bytes)
    15	#   state    .run/karpathy-surgical/<key>.jsonl — one small file per task, so
    16	#            the total resets when the task changes; the directory keeps the
    17	#            20 most recently written files and deletes older ones
    18	#   summary  .run/karpathy-surgical-summary.json
    19	#            {task, lines, threshold, over, updated_at}, rewritten atomically
    20	#            after each counted write; the review's SURGICAL axis reads it
    21	#   legacy   .run/karpathy-task-state.jsonl (the old session-long total) and
    22	#            its two perf caches are deleted on the first run of this layout
    23	#
    24	# Over `karpathy_principles.diff_lines_per_task` (default 100) it prints the
    25	# `[karpathy-surgical-warn]` stderr line and appends a trajectory event
    26	# (karpathy-check.payload.schema.json). Non-blocking: always exits 0. The
    27	# master switch `karpathy_principles.surgical_diff_warning` is read through
    28	# loa_knob (explicit key, else the loa.profile default; `lean` turns it off).
    29	#
    30	# Safety (NFR-Sec-1): tool_input.content / new_string never reach state,
    31	# summary or trajectory — only line counts, the file path (JSON-encoded by
    32	# jq) and the sanitised key. Missing jq or yq, a missing config or a
    33	# malformed payload is a silent no-op. A symlinked state directory or state
    34	# file is not written through.
    35	#
    36	# Seams (tests): LOA_CONFIG_OVERRIDE (config), KARPATHY_STATE_DIR,
    37	# KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE, KARPATHY_LEGACY_STATE, KARPATHY_TRAJECTORY_DIR,
    38	# KARPATHY_CHECKPOINT_CMD (default .claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh, which
    39	# itself honours LOA_RUN_DIR), KARPATHY_STATE_KEEP (default 20).
    40	#
    41	# Design note: the session-long state file grew without bound, which is what
    42	# the earlier perf passes (config-token and state-aggregate caches) existed
    43	# to absorb. Per-task files are small and rotated, so the hook reads them in
    44	# full each time and those caches are gone.
    45	
    46	set -uo pipefail
    47	umask 077
    48	export LC_ALL=C
    49	
    50	_src="${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"
    51	_src_dir="${_src%/*}"
    52	[[ "$_src_dir" == "$_src" ]] && _src_dir="."
    53	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$_src_dir" && pwd)"
    54	REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../../.." && pwd)"
    55	DEFAULT_CONFIG="$REPO_ROOT/.loa.config.yaml"
    56	CONFIG="${LOA_CONFIG_OVERRIDE:-$DEFAULT_CONFIG}"
    57	DEFAULT_STATE_DIR="$REPO_ROOT/.run/karpathy-surgical"
    58	STATE_DIR="${KARPATHY_STATE_DIR:-$DEFAULT_STATE_DIR}"
    59	SUMMARY="${KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE:-$REPO_ROOT/.run/karpathy-surgical-summary.json}"
    60	LEGACY="${KARPATHY_LEGACY_STATE:-$REPO_ROOT/.run/karpathy-task-state.jsonl}"
    61	TRAJ_DIR="${KARPATHY_TRAJECTORY_DIR:-$REPO_ROOT/grimoires/loa/a2a/trajectory}"
    62	CHECKPOINT="${KARPATHY_CHECKPOINT_CMD:-$REPO_ROOT/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh}"
    63	KEEP="${KARPATHY_STATE_KEEP:-20}"
    64	[[ "$KEEP" =~ ^[0-9]{1,4}$ && "$KEEP" -ge 1 ]] || KEEP=20
    65	
    66	command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 0
    67	command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 0
    68	[[ -f "$CONFIG" ]] || exit 0
    69	
    70	# --- master switch and threshold (loa_knob: explicit key > profile > fallback)
    71	# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh
    72	source "$REPO_ROOT/.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh" 2>/dev/null || exit 0
    73	if [[ "$CONFIG" != "$DEFAULT_CONFIG" ]]; then export LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE="$CONFIG"; fi
    74	switch="$(loa_knob karpathy_principles.surgical_diff_warning true 2>/dev/null)"
    75	case "$switch" in
    76	    false|False|FALSE|0|no|No|NO|off|Off|OFF) exit 0 ;;
    77	esac
    78	THRESHOLD="$(loa_knob karpathy_principles.diff_lines_per_task 100 2>/dev/null)"
    79	[[ "$THRESHOLD" =~ ^[0-9]{1,9}$ ]] || THRESHOLD=100
    80	THRESHOLD=$((10#$THRESHOLD))
    81	
    82	# --- payload: one jq, one JSON-encoded field per line (no raw newlines) ---
    83	payload="$(cat)"
    84	[[ -n "$payload" ]] || exit 0
    85	fields="$(printf '%s' "$payload" | jq -r '
    86	    def slines: if . == "" then 1 else (split("\n") | length) end;
    87	    def jl: if type == "array" or type == "object"
    88	            then (if length == 0 then 1 else 2 + ([.[] | jl] | add) end)
    89	            else 1 end;
    90	    def count: if . == null or . == false then 0 elif type == "string" then slines else jl end;
    91	    select(type == "object") |
    92	    (.tool_name // "" | if type == "string" then . else tojson end) as $tn |
    93	    ([($tn | tojson),
    94	      (if $tn == "Write" then (.tool_input.content | count)
    95	       elif ($tn == "Edit" or $tn == "NotebookEdit") then (.tool_input.new_string | count)
    96	       else 0 end | tostring),
    97	      ((.tool_input.file_path // "<unknown>") | (if type == "string" then . else tojson end) | tojson),
    98	      ((.session_id // "") | (if type == "string" then . else "" end) | tojson),
    99	      (now | todate)] | .[])
   100	' 2>/dev/null | head -5)" || exit 0
   101	{
   102	    IFS= read -r TOOL_JSON
   103	    IFS= read -r LINES
   104	    IFS= read -r FILE_JSON
   105	    IFS= read -r PAYLOAD_SID_JSON
   106	    IFS= read -r TS
   107	} <<< "$fields"
   108	case "${TOOL_JSON:-}" in
   109	    '"Write"') TOOL_NAME=Write ;;
   110	    '"Edit"') TOOL_NAME=Edit ;;
   111	    '"NotebookEdit"') TOOL_NAME=NotebookEdit ;;
   112	    *) exit 0 ;;
   113	esac
   114	[[ "${LINES:-}" =~ ^[0-9]{1,12}$ ]] || exit 0
   115	[[ -n "${FILE_JSON:-}" && -n "${TS:-}" ]] || exit 0
   116	
   117	# --- the key ------------------------------------------------------------------
   118	_sanitise() {  # stdin-free: $1 → ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ (may print empty)
   119	    local s
   120	    s="$(printf '%s' "$1" | tr -c 'A-Za-z0-9._-' '_' | cut -c1-128)"
   121	    [[ "$s" == .* ]] && s="_${s#.}"
   122	    printf '%s' "$s"
   123	}
   124	payload_sid="$(printf '%s' "${PAYLOAD_SID_JSON:-\"\"}" | jq -r '.' 2>/dev/null)" || payload_sid=""
   125	SESSION="${payload_sid:-${LOA_SESSION_ID:-}}"
   126	[[ -n "$SESSION" ]] || SESSION="${USER:-unknown}-${TS:0:4}${TS:5:2}${TS:8:2}"
   127	SESSION_JSON="$(jq -cn --arg s "$SESSION" '$s')"
   128	
   129	task_raw=""
   130	if [[ -f "$CHECKPOINT" ]]; then
   131	    task_raw="$(bash "$CHECKPOINT" read --json 2>/dev/null \
   132	        | jq -r '[.checkpoint.task?, .checkpoint.sprint?, .sprint?] | map(select(type == "string" and . != ""))
   133	                  | .[0] // empty | gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9._-]"; "_")' 2>/dev/null \
   134	        | head -1)" || task_raw=""
   135	fi
   136	KEY="$(_sanitise "$task_raw")"
   137	[[ -n "$KEY" ]] || KEY="$(_sanitise "$SESSION")"
   138	[[ -n "$KEY" ]] || KEY="session-unknown"
   139	
   140	# --- legacy layout: deleted on the first run under this one -------------------
   141	if [[ -e "$LEGACY" || -L "$LEGACY" ]]; then
   142	    rm -f -- "$LEGACY" 2>/dev/null || true
   143	    if [[ "$STATE_DIR" == "$DEFAULT_STATE_DIR" ]]; then
   144	        rm -f -- "$REPO_ROOT/.run/perf-cache/karpathy-state.v1.agg" \
   145	                 "$REPO_ROOT/.run/perf-cache/karpathy-config.v1.tokens" 2>/dev/null || true
   146	    fi
   147	fi
   148	
   149	# --- append to the task's file ------------------------------------------------
   150	[[ -L "$STATE_DIR" ]] && exit 0
   151	[[ -d "$STATE_DIR" ]] || mkdir -p "$STATE_DIR" 2>/dev/null || exit 0
   152	TASK_FILE="$STATE_DIR/$KEY.jsonl"
   153	[[ -L "$TASK_FILE" ]] && exit 0
   154	
   155	PRIOR=0
   156	if [[ -f "$TASK_FILE" ]]; then
   157	    # Tolerant of malformed lines: sums every `"lines_changed":<int>` it finds.
   158	    PRIOR="$(awk -F'"lines_changed":' '/"lines_changed":/ { sum += $2 + 0 } END { print sum + 0 }' "$TASK_FILE" 2>/dev/null)" || PRIOR=0
   159	    [[ "$PRIOR" =~ ^[0-9]{1,15}$ ]] || PRIOR=0
   160	fi
   161	RUNNING=$((PRIOR + LINES))
   162	
   163	printf '{"ts":"%s","tool":"%s","file":%s,"lines_changed":%s,"running_total":%s,"session_id":%s,"task":"%s"}\n' \
   164	    "$TS" "$TOOL_NAME" "$FILE_JSON" "$LINES" "$RUNNING" "$SESSION_JSON" "$KEY" >> "$TASK_FILE" 2>/dev/null || exit 0
   165	
   166	# Keep the KEEP most recently written task files (names are sanitised: no
   167	# whitespace, no leading dot, so the glob and the ls listing are exact).
   168	n=0
   169	while IFS= read -r old; do
   170	    n=$((n + 1))
   171	    if (( n > KEEP )) && [[ "$old" != "$TASK_FILE" && ! -L "$old" ]]; then
   172	        rm -f -- "$old" 2>/dev/null || true
   173	    fi
   174	done < <(ls -1t -- "$STATE_DIR"/*.jsonl 2>/dev/null)
   175	
   176	# --- summary (atomic) ---------------------------------------------------------
   177	OVER=false
   178	(( RUNNING > THRESHOLD )) && OVER=true
   179	sum_dir="${SUMMARY%/*}"
   180	[[ "$sum_dir" == "$SUMMARY" ]] && sum_dir="."
   181	if [[ -d "$sum_dir" ]] || mkdir -p "$sum_dir" 2>/dev/null; then
   182	    tmp="$SUMMARY.tmp.$$"
   183	    if printf '{"task":"%s","lines":%s,"threshold":%s,"over":%s,"updated_at":"%s"}\n' \
   184	            "$KEY" "$RUNNING" "$THRESHOLD" "$OVER" "$TS" > "$tmp" 2>/dev/null; then
   185	        mv -f -- "$tmp" "$SUMMARY" 2>/dev/null || rm -f -- "$tmp" 2>/dev/null
   186	    else
   187	        rm -f -- "$tmp" 2>/dev/null
   188	    fi
   189	fi
   190	
   191	# --- warning + trajectory event -----------------------------------------------
   192	if [[ "$OVER" == "true" ]]; then
   193	    echo "[karpathy-surgical-warn] Session diff total ${RUNNING} lines exceeds threshold ${THRESHOLD}. Karpathy principle 3 (Surgical Changes): verify every changed line traces to the stated task. State: $TASK_FILE" >&2
   194	
   195	    counts="$(jq -nr --rawfile s "$TASK_FILE" '
   196	        ($s | split("\n") | map(select(length > 0))) as $l |
   197	        (try ([$l[] | fromjson | .file // empty] | unique | length) catch 0) as $f |
   198	        "\($f) \($l | length)"' 2>/dev/null)" || counts="0 0"
   199	    FILES_MOD="${counts%% *}"; TOOL_CALLS="${counts##* }"
   200	    [[ "$FILES_MOD" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || FILES_MOD=0
   201	    [[ "$TOOL_CALLS" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || TOOL_CALLS=0
   202	    [[ -d "$TRAJ_DIR" ]] || mkdir -p "$TRAJ_DIR" 2>/dev/null || exit 0
   203	    printf '{"phase":"karpathy_check","principle":"surgical_changes","timestamp":"%s","files_modified":%s,"lines_total":%s,"threshold":%s,"verdict":"warn","tool_call_count":%s,"session_id":%s}\n' \
   204	        "$TS" "$FILES_MOD" "$RUNNING" "$THRESHOLD" "$TOOL_CALLS" "$SESSION_JSON" \
   205	        >> "$TRAJ_DIR/karpathy-${TS:0:10}.jsonl" 2>/dev/null || true
   206	fi
   207	
   208	exit 0

    74	switch="$(loa_knob karpathy_principles.surgical_diff_warning true 2>/dev/null)"
    75	case "$switch" in
    76	    false|False|FALSE|0|no|No|NO|off|Off|OFF) exit 0 ;;
    77	esac
    78	THRESHOLD="$(loa_knob karpathy_principles.diff_lines_per_task 100 2>/dev/null)"
    79	[[ "$THRESHOLD" =~ ^[0-9]{1,9}$ ]] || THRESHOLD=100
    80	THRESHOLD=$((10#$THRESHOLD))
    81	
    82	# --- payload: one jq, one JSON-encoded field per line (no raw newlines) ---
    83	payload="$(cat)"
    84	[[ -n "$payload" ]] || exit 0
    85	fields="$(printf '%s' "$payload" | jq -r '
    86	    def slines: if . == "" then 1 else (split("\n") | length) end;
    87	    def jl: if type == "array" or type == "object"
    88	            then (if length == 0 then 1 else 2 + ([.[] | jl] | add) end)
    89	            else 1 end;

    91	    select(type == "object") |

    93	    ([($tn | tojson),
    94	      (if $tn == "Write" then (.tool_input.content | count)
    95	       elif ($tn == "Edit" or $tn == "NotebookEdit") then (.tool_input.new_string | count)

    97	      ((.tool_input.file_path // "<unknown>") | (if type == "string" then . else tojson end) | tojson),
    98	      ((.session_id // "") | (if type == "string" then . else "" end) | tojson),
    99	      (now | todate)] | .[])
   100	' 2>/dev/null | head -5)" || exit 0
   101	{
   102	    IFS= read -r TOOL_JSON
   103	    IFS= read -r LINES
   104	    IFS= read -r FILE_JSON
   105	    IFS= read -r PAYLOAD_SID_JSON
   106	    IFS= read -r TS
   107	} <<< "$fields"
   108	case "${TOOL_JSON:-}" in
   109	    '"Write"') TOOL_NAME=Write ;;
   110	    '"Edit"') TOOL_NAME=Edit ;;
   111	    '"NotebookEdit"') TOOL_NAME=NotebookEdit ;;

   113	esac
   114	[[ "${LINES:-}" =~ ^[0-9]{1,12}$ ]] || exit 0
   115	[[ -n "${FILE_JSON:-}" && -n "${TS:-}" ]] || exit 0
   116	
   117	# --- the key ------------------------------------------------------------------
   118	_sanitise() {  # stdin-free: $1 → ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ (may print empty)
   119	    local s
   120	    s="$(printf '%s' "$1" | tr -c 'A-Za-z0-9._-' '_' | cut -c1-128)"
   121	    [[ "$s" == .* ]] && s="_${s#.}"
   122	    printf '%s' "$s"
   123	}
   124	payload_sid="$(printf '%s' "${PAYLOAD_SID_JSON:-\"\"}" | jq -r '.' 2>/dev/null)" || payload_sid=""
   125	SESSION="${payload_sid:-${LOA_SESSION_ID:-}}"
   126	[[ -n "$SESSION" ]] || SESSION="${USER:-unknown}-${TS:0:4}${TS:5:2}${TS:8:2}"
   127	SESSION_JSON="$(jq -cn --arg s "$SESSION" '$s')"
   128	
   129	task_raw=""
   130	if [[ -f "$CHECKPOINT" ]]; then
   131	    task_raw="$(bash "$CHECKPOINT" read --json 2>/dev/null \
   132	        | jq -r '[.checkpoint.task?, .checkpoint.sprint?, .sprint?] | map(select(type == "string" and . != ""))
   133	                  | .[0] // empty | gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9._-]"; "_")' 2>/dev/null \
   134	        | head -1)" || task_raw=""
   135	fi
   136	KEY="$(_sanitise "$task_raw")"
   137	[[ -n "$KEY" ]] || KEY="$(_sanitise "$SESSION")"
   138	[[ -n "$KEY" ]] || KEY="session-unknown"
   139	
   140	# --- legacy layout: deleted on the first run under this one -------------------
   141	if [[ -e "$LEGACY" || -L "$LEGACY" ]]; then
   142	    rm -f -- "$LEGACY" 2>/dev/null || true
   143	    if [[ "$STATE_DIR" == "$DEFAULT_STATE_DIR" ]]; then
   144	        rm -f -- "$REPO_ROOT/.run/perf-cache/karpathy-state.v1.agg" \
   145	                 "$REPO_ROOT/.run/perf-cache/karpathy-config.v1.tokens" 2>/dev/null || true
   146	    fi
   147	fi
   148	
   149	# --- append to the task's file ------------------------------------------------
   150	[[ -L "$STATE_DIR" ]] && exit 0
   151	[[ -d "$STATE_DIR" ]] || mkdir -p "$STATE_DIR" 2>/dev/null || exit 0
   152	TASK_FILE="$STATE_DIR/$KEY.jsonl"
   153	[[ -L "$TASK_FILE" ]] && exit 0
   154	
   155	PRIOR=0
   156	if [[ -f "$TASK_FILE" ]]; then
   157	    # Tolerant of malformed lines: sums every `"lines_changed":<int>` it finds.
   158	    PRIOR="$(awk -F'"lines_changed":' '/"lines_changed":/ { sum += $2 + 0 } END { print sum + 0 }' "$TASK_FILE" 2>/dev/null)" || PRIOR=0
   159	    [[ "$PRIOR" =~ ^[0-9]{1,15}$ ]] || PRIOR=0
   160	fi
   161	RUNNING=$((PRIOR + LINES))
   162	
   163	printf '{"ts":"%s","tool":"%s","file":%s,"lines_changed":%s,"running_total":%s,"session_id":%s,"task":"%s"}\n' \
   164	    "$TS" "$TOOL_NAME" "$FILE_JSON" "$LINES" "$RUNNING" "$SESSION_JSON" "$KEY" >> "$TASK_FILE" 2>/dev/null || exit 0
   165	
   166	# Keep the KEEP most recently written task files (names are sanitised: no
   167	# whitespace, no leading dot, so the glob and the ls listing are exact).

   169	while IFS= read -r old; do
   170	    n=$((n + 1))

   172	        rm -f -- "$old" 2>/dev/null || true
   173	    fi

   178	(( RUNNING > THRESHOLD )) && OVER=true
   179	sum_dir="${SUMMARY%/*}"
   180	[[ "$sum_dir" == "$SUMMARY" ]] && sum_dir="."
   181	if [[ -d "$sum_dir" ]] || mkdir -p "$sum_dir" 2>/dev/null; then
   182	    tmp="$SUMMARY.tmp.$$"
   183	    if printf '{"task":"%s","lines":%s,"threshold":%s,"over":%s,"updated_at":"%s"}\n' \
   184	            "$KEY" "$RUNNING" "$THRESHOLD" "$OVER" "$TS" > "$tmp" 2>/dev/null; then
   185	        mv -f -- "$tmp" "$SUMMARY" 2>/dev/null || rm -f -- "$tmp" 2>/dev/null
   186	    else
   187	        rm -f -- "$tmp" 2>/dev/null
   188	    fi
   189	fi

   191	# --- warning + trajectory event -----------------------------------------------
   192	if [[ "$OVER" == "true" ]]; then
   193	    echo "[karpathy-surgical-warn] Session diff total ${RUNNING} lines exceeds threshold ${THRESHOLD}. Karpathy principle 3 (Surgical Changes): verify every changed line traces to the stated task. State: $TASK_FILE" >&2

   196	        ($s | split("\n") | map(select(length > 0))) as $l |

   202	    [[ -d "$TRAJ_DIR" ]] || mkdir -p "$TRAJ_DIR" 2>/dev/null || exit 0
   203	    printf '{"phase":"karpathy_check","principle":"surgical_changes","timestamp":"%s","files_modified":%s,"lines_total":%s,"threshold":%s,"verdict":"warn","tool_call_count":%s,"session_id":%s}\n' \
   204	        "$TS" "$FILES_MOD" "$RUNNING" "$THRESHOLD" "$TOOL_CALLS" "$SESSION_JSON" \
   205	        >> "$TRAJ_DIR/karpathy-${TS:0:10}.jsonl" 2>/dev/null || true
   206	fi

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# implement-gate.sh — Dual-mode compliance hook for App Zone writes (FR-7)
     4	# =============================================================================
     5	# Checks whether Write/Edit to App Zone files occurs within an active
     6	# /implement or /bug skill invocation.
     7	#
     8	# Modes (cycle-129 D-4.1, DEC-0163; .loa.config.yaml implement_gate.mode):
     9	#   ask (default; unset or any other value): an unsanctioned App-Zone write asks,
    10	#       exactly as before, and now logs one row (decision "ask").
    11	#   telemetry: an unsanctioned App-Zone write logs one row (action "telemetry",
    12	#       decision "outside_run") and is allowed silently.
    13	#   deny: an unsanctioned App-Zone write is DENIED when the run position is
    14	#       known: .run/sprint-plan-state.json parses and its derived_at is within
    15	#       run_mode.stale_hours (12). The gate is a fence only in this mode. An
    16	#       unknown position (cache missing, not derived, stale or unparseable)
    17	#       falls back to ask (decision "unknown_position"), never to allow.
    18	# Sanction (any mode; first match wins; one row each, action "allow"):
    19	#   sanctioned_run    — the heuristic below: a fresh RUNNING cache, and its
    20	#                       derived_at (when present) within run_mode.stale_hours
    21	#   sanctioned_marker — .run/implement-active.json {skill: implement|bug, sprint,
    22	#                       started_at} with started_at within two hours (written by
    23	#                       `run-checkpoint.sh mark`, removed by `unmark`); a stale or
    24	#                       malformed marker logs decision "stale_marker" and does not sanction
    25	#   override          — LOA_IMPLEMENT_GATE_OVERRIDE=1 in the hook's environment
    26	# Rows go to .run/audit.jsonl as {ts, hook: "implement-gate", action, decision,
    27	# mode, path} with path control-stripped and cut to 256 bytes; LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY=1
    28	# adds replay: true to every row this gate writes (DEC-0167).
    29	#
    30	# Claims modifier (implement_gate.claims: authoritative; the legacy
    31	# implement_gate.mode: authoritative means mode ask + claims authoritative):
    32	#   reads tool_input.active_skill from hook stdin. The PreToolUse
    33	#      payload carries no harness-set skill field (cycle-126 D-4.4) and tool_input
    34	#      is model-authored, so nothing in .run/ selects this modifier.
    35	#      TIGHTEN-ONLY (sprint-250 audit n17/n18): the model-authored claim can only
    36	#      add an ask, never grant an allow. A claimed implementation skill falls
    37	#      through to the heuristic exactly like an absent field; a claimed
    38	#      non-implementation skill asks (or, under deny with a known position and no
    39	#      sanction, is denied) and logs compliance.mode.model_signal to
    40	#      .run/audit.jsonl (plain hook log, not the signed audit_emit chain). Every
    41	#      claim leaves one row per invocation: decision "ask"/"deny" for a non-implementation
    42	#      claim, decision "heuristic" for an implementation claim (run-2 finding 6).
    43	#
    44	# `implement-gate.sh --effective-mode [CONFIG]` prints the effective mode (and the
    45	# claims modifier) without reading stdin — the /loa Gate line.
    46	#
    47	# Evidence recorder (cycle-126 D-4.4): a lead-session payload carrying
    48	# tool_input.active_skill records active_skill_seen_at once in
    49	# .run/platform-features.json. It is evidence only and never changes the mode.
    50	#
    51	# Failure mode: FAIL-ASK for App Zone writes (not fail-open). A payload jq cannot
    52	# parse (or no jq), or a file_path that cannot be canonicalised, asks too (run-2
    53	# findings 1/5). The path is tool_input.file_path, or tool_input.notebook_path for
    54	# NotebookEdit; a relative path resolves from the payload's cwd, else PROJECT_ROOT
    55	# (run-3 finding 6). The zone test ORs a physical form (symlinks followed) and a
    56	# logical form (symlinks kept) and matches a lowercased copy (run-3 findings 1/2).
    57	# Root: PROJECT_ROOT, else CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, else this script's location
    58	# (<root>/.claude/hooks/compliance/), never the process cwd, which follows
    59	# Claude's `cd` (audit MED-001); RUN_DIR defaults to <root>/.run.
    60	# Trust inputs: a write to .run/state.json, .run/sprint-plan-state.json,
    61	# .run/simstim-state.json, .run/platform-features.json, .run/audit.jsonl,
    62	# .run/implement-active.json or .loa.config.yaml asks in every mode and under
    63	# every sanction, and logs compliance.state_write (run-3 finding 3).
    64	# Other non-App-Zone writes always allowed.
    65	#
    66	# Output (Claude Code PreToolUse contract, sprint-250 audit n20): allow = silent
    67	# exit 0 with empty stdout; ask = exit 0 with
    68	#   {"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","permissionDecision":"ask","permissionDecisionReason":"…"}}
    69	# deny = the same shape with "permissionDecision":"deny".
    70	# A top-level "decision" accepts approve|block only, so "ask" never goes there.
    71	# file_path and active_skill reach stderr only through strip_controls (n21;
    72	# run-2 findings 3/12; run-3 finding 5): cut to 256 bytes without splitting a
    73	# character, then C0 and DEL, UTF-8 C1 controls and the Unicode format/bidi/tag
    74	# code points are removed to a fixed point. Audit rows record the RAW values cut
    75	# the same way and written with jq -a, so every non-ASCII code point is \uXXXX:
    76	# faithful (implement+U+200B logs as implement\u200b) and terminal-safe (run-3 finding 4).
    77	#
    78	# IMPORTANT: No set -euo pipefail — hook must never crash-block.
    79	# Parse/read errors on App Zone writes → ask (not allow).
    80	#
    81	# Part of cycle-049/050: Upstream Platform Alignment (FR-7)
    82	# Red Team findings addressed: ATK-005 (state tampering), ATK-006 (fail-open),
    83	#   ATK-007 (prompt injection via file path)
    84	# Sprint-108 T4.4: Dual-mode (authoritative + heuristic)
    85	# Sprint-108 T4.5: Path normalization
    86	# =============================================================================
    87	
    88	# Read tool input from stdin (not for --effective-mode, which reads no payload)
    89	input=""
    90	if [[ "${1:-}" != "--effective-mode" ]]; then
    91	    input=$(cat 2>/dev/null) || input=""
    92	fi
    93	
    94	# The ask reply; jq builds it so any reason is a well-formed JSON string (run-3 finding 7); the printf literal is only
    95	# for the jq-missing branch, whose reason is a fixed string
    96	emit_ask() {
    97	    if command -v jq &>/dev/null; then
    98	        jq -nc --arg r "$1" '{hookSpecificOutput:{hookEventName:"PreToolUse",permissionDecision:"ask",permissionDecisionReason:$r}}'
    99	    else
   100	        printf '{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","permissionDecision":"ask","permissionDecisionReason":"%s"}}\n' "$1"
   101	    fi
   102	}
   103	
   104	# Byte sequences strip_controls removes: UTF-8 C1 controls (C2 80..C2 9F) and the format/bidi code points
   105	# U+200B-U+200F, U+2028-U+202E, U+2060-U+2064, U+2066-U+206F, U+FEFF, U+00AD, U+061C, U+180E, U+FE00-U+FE0F,
   106	# U+FFF9-U+FFFB and the tag characters U+E0001, U+E0020-U+E007F (run-3 finding 5); each sequence starts with a lead
   107	# byte, so a byte-wise match never lands inside another character
   108	# printf -v keeps this portable (no GNU-sed \x); built on first use, not on every Write/Edit (BB-008)
   109	_IG_STRIP_SEQS=()
   110	_ig_strip_seqs_init() {
   111	    local _ig_i _ig_hex _ig_seq
   112	    for (( _ig_i = 128; _ig_i < 160; _ig_i++ )); do
   113	        printf -v _ig_hex '%02x' "$_ig_i"; printf -v _ig_seq "\\xc2\\x${_ig_hex}"; _IG_STRIP_SEQS+=("$_ig_seq")
   114	    done
   115	    for _ig_hex in 8b 8c 8d 8e 8f a8 a9 aa ab ac ad ae; do
   116	        printf -v _ig_seq "\\xe2\\x80\\x${_ig_hex}"; _IG_STRIP_SEQS+=("$_ig_seq")
   117	    done
   118	    for _ig_hex in a0 a1 a2 a3 a4 a6 a7 a8 a9 aa ab ac ad ae af; do
   119	        printf -v _ig_seq "\\xe2\\x81\\x${_ig_hex}"; _IG_STRIP_SEQS+=("$_ig_seq")
   120	    done
   121	    for _ig_seq in '\xef\xbb\xbf' '\xc2\xad' '\xd8\x9c' '\xe1\xa0\x8e' '\xef\xbf\xb9' '\xef\xbf\xba' '\xef\xbf\xbb' '\xf3\xa0\x80\x81'; do
   122	        printf -v _ig_seq "$_ig_seq"; _IG_STRIP_SEQS+=("$_ig_seq")
   123	    done
   124	    for (( _ig_i = 128; _ig_i < 144; _ig_i++ )); do   # U+FE00-U+FE0F = EF B8 80..EF B8 8F
   125	        printf -v _ig_hex '%02x' "$_ig_i"; printf -v _ig_seq "\\xef\\xb8\\x${_ig_hex}"; _IG_STRIP_SEQS+=("$_ig_seq")
   126	    done
   127	    for (( _ig_i = 160; _ig_i < 192; _ig_i++ )); do   # U+E0020-U+E003F = F3 A0 80 A0..F3 A0 80 BF
   128	        printf -v _ig_hex '%02x' "$_ig_i"; printf -v _ig_seq "\\xf3\\xa0\\x80\\x${_ig_hex}"; _IG_STRIP_SEQS+=("$_ig_seq")
   129	    done
   130	    for (( _ig_i = 128; _ig_i < 192; _ig_i++ )); do   # U+E0040-U+E007F = F3 A0 81 80..F3 A0 81 BF
   131	        printf -v _ig_hex '%02x' "$_ig_i"; printf -v _ig_seq "\\xf3\\xa0\\x81\\x${_ig_hex}"; _IG_STRIP_SEQS+=("$_ig_seq")
   132	    done
   133	}
   134	
   135	# Sets the variable named $1 to at most 256 bytes of $2, never ending inside a UTF-8 character: a trailing lead byte
   136	# whose sequence the cut left short, or stray continuation bytes, are dropped (run-3 finding 5; jq would read a split
   137	# character as U+FFFD). printf -v, not $(...), so a trailing newline in a raw value survives into the audit row
   138	cut_utf8_256() {
   139	    local LC_ALL=C
   140	    local _c_s=${2:0:256} _c_n _c_i _c_b _c_need
   141	    _c_n=${#_c_s}
   142	    for (( _c_i = _c_n - 1; _c_i >= 0 && _c_i >= _c_n - 4; _c_i-- )); do
   143	        printf -v _c_b '%d' "'${_c_s:_c_i:1}"
   144	        (( _c_b >= 128 && _c_b < 192 )) && continue   # continuation byte: keep walking back to its lead
   145	        if (( _c_b < 128 )); then _c_need=1; elif (( _c_b < 224 )); then _c_need=2; elif (( _c_b < 240 )); then _c_need=3; else _c_need=4; fi
   146	        if (( _c_n - _c_i < _c_need )); then _c_s=${_c_s:0:_c_i}          # the cut left this character short
   147	        elif (( _c_n - _c_i > _c_need )); then _c_s=${_c_s:0:_c_i+_c_need}   # continuation bytes after a complete character are stray
   148	        fi
   149	        printf -v "$1" '%s' "$_c_s"
   150	        return 0
   151	    done
   152	    printf -v "$1" '%s' "${_c_s:0:_c_i+1}"   # only continuation bytes at the end: drop them
   153	}
   154	
   155	# Display copy of a model-authored string: cut to 256 bytes first (the fixed point below then costs at most a few
   156	# passes over a short string), then C0 and DEL, then the sequences above byte-wise until nothing changes (deleting
   157	# one sequence can join its neighbours into another: C2 C2 9B 9B)
   158	strip_controls() {
   159	    local LC_ALL=C s prev seq
   160	    cut_utf8_256 s "$1"
   161	    s=$(printf '%s' "$s" | tr -d '\000-\037\177')
   162	    (( ${#_IG_STRIP_SEQS[@]} )) || _ig_strip_seqs_init
   163	    while :; do
   164	        prev=$s
   165	        for seq in "${_IG_STRIP_SEQS[@]}"; do s=${s//"$seq"/}; done
   166	        [[ "$s" == "$prev" ]] && break
   167	    done
   168	    printf '%s' "$s"
   169	}
   170	
   171	# The root never follows the process cwd, which follows Claude's `cd` (sprint-250 audit MED-001): PROJECT_ROOT, then
   172	# the harness's CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR (it stays at the session's project root), then this script's own location
   173	# (<root>/.claude/hooks/compliance/)
   174	PROJECT_ROOT="${PROJECT_ROOT:-${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../../.." 2>/dev/null && pwd)}}"
   175	RUN_DIR="${RUN_DIR:-$PROJECT_ROOT/.run}"
   176	FEATURES_FILE="$RUN_DIR/platform-features.json"
   177	
   178	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   179	# Mode and claims (cycle-129 D-4.1): one yq call, read only when a decision
   180	# needs it. Unset, unreadable or unknown values are ask; the legacy
   181	# mode: authoritative is ask + claims: authoritative. run_mode.stale_hours
   182	# bounds derived_at (positive integer, default 12).
   183	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   184	gate_mode="ask"
   185	gate_claims="plain"
   186	gate_stale_hours=12
   187	load_gate_config() {
   188	    local cfg="${1:-$PROJECT_ROOT/.loa.config.yaml}" raw m c s
   189	    command -v yq &>/dev/null && command -v jq &>/dev/null && [[ -f "$cfg" ]] || return 0
   190	    # mikefarah yq v4 first; the python yq wrapper (jq syntax, JSON out) second
   191	    raw=$(yq -o json -I 0 '{"m": .implement_gate.mode, "c": .implement_gate.claims, "s": .run_mode.stale_hours}' "$cfg" 2>/dev/null) \
   192	        || raw=$(yq -c '{"m": .implement_gate.mode, "c": .implement_gate.claims, "s": .run_mode.stale_hours}' "$cfg" 2>/dev/null) \
   193	        || return 0
   194	    m=$(jq -r '.m | strings' <<<"$raw" 2>/dev/null) || m=""
   195	    c=$(jq -r '.c | strings' <<<"$raw" 2>/dev/null) || c=""
   196	    s=$(jq -r '.s | numbers | tostring' <<<"$raw" 2>/dev/null) || s=""
   197	    case "$m" in
   198	        ask|telemetry|deny) gate_mode="$m" ;;
   199	        authoritative) gate_claims="authoritative" ;;
   200	    esac
   201	    [[ "$c" == "authoritative" ]] && gate_claims="authoritative"
   202	    if [[ "$s" =~ ^[0-9]{1,4}$ ]] && (( 10#$s > 0 && 10#$s <= 8760 )); then gate_stale_hours=$(( 10#$s )); fi
   203	    return 0
   204	}
   205	
   206	if [[ "${1:-}" == "--effective-mode" ]]; then
   207	    load_gate_config "${2:-}"
   208	    if [[ "$gate_claims" == "authoritative" ]]; then echo "$gate_mode (claims: authoritative)"; else echo "$gate_mode"; fi
   209	    exit 0
   210	fi
   211	
   212	# Row helpers: LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY=1 marks every row this gate writes (DEC-0167)
   213	_ig_replay_json='{}'
   214	[[ "${LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY:-}" == "1" ]] && _ig_replay_json='{"replay":true}'

273	JQ_DEFS='
274	def	epoch:	if	type	==	"string"	then	(sub("\\.[0-9]+Z$";	"Z")	|	try	fromdateiso8601	catch	null)	else	null	end;
275	def	fresh($now;	$win):	epoch	as	$t	|	$t	!=	null	and	($now	-	$t)	<=	$win	and	($t	-	$now)	<=	300;
276	def	recompute($rounds;	$reset):
277	($rounds
278	|	map(select($reset	==	null	or	((.ts	//	"")	>	$reset)))
279	|	sort_by([(.ts	//	""),	.round,	(if	.gate	==	"review"	then	0	else	1	end)])
280	|	map(select(.approved	|	not)))	as	$nr
281	|	reduce	$nr[]	as	$r	({cycle:	0,	same:	0,	hash:	null,	np:	0,	lc:	null};
282	.cycle	+=	1
283	|	(if	$r.hash	!=	"none"	and	$r.hash	==	.hash	then	.same	+=	1	else	.same	=	1	|	.hash	=	$r.hash	end)
284	|	($r.counts	|	tojson)	as	$c
285	|	(if	.lc	!=	null	and	.lc	==	$c	then	.np	+=	1	else	.np	=	0	end)
286	|	.lc	=	$c);
287	def	skeleton($th;	$ts):
288	{state:	"CLOSED",
289	triggers:	{same_issue:	{count:	0,	threshold:	$th.same,	last_hash:	null},
290	no_progress:	{count:	0,	threshold:	$th.np},
291	cycle_count:	{current:	0,	limit:	$th.cycles},
292	timeout:	{started:	$ts,	limit_hours:	$th.hours}},
293	history:	[]};
294	def	merge_breaker($rc;	$th;	$ts):
295	(if	type	==	"object"	then	.	else	skeleton($th;	$ts)	end)
296	|	.triggers	=	(.triggers	//	{})
297	|	.triggers.cycle_count.current	=	([(.triggers.cycle_count.current	//	0),	$rc.cycle]	|	max)
298	|	(if	$rc.same	>	(.triggers.same_issue.count	//	0)
299	then	.triggers.same_issue.count	=	$rc.same	|	.triggers.same_issue.last_hash	=	$rc.hash	else	.	end)
300	|	(if	$rc.np	>	(.triggers.no_progress.count	//	0)	or	(.triggers.no_progress.last_counts	==	null	and	$rc.lc	!=	null)
301	then	.triggers.no_progress.count	=	([(.triggers.no_progress.count	//	0),	$rc.np]	|	max)
302	|	.triggers.no_progress.last_counts	=	$rc.lc	else	.	end)
303	|	(	if	(.triggers.same_issue.count	//	0)	>=	(.triggers.same_issue.threshold	//	$th.same)
304	then	["same_issue",	"same	issue	hash	repeated	\(.triggers.same_issue.count)	times	(derived	from	the	feedback	history)"]
305	elif	(.triggers.no_progress.count	//	0)	>=	(.triggers.no_progress.threshold	//	$th.np)
306	then	["no_progress",	"counts	unchanged	for	\(.triggers.no_progress.count)	consecutive	rounds	(derived	from	the	feedback	history)"]
307	elif	(.triggers.cycle_count.current	//	0)	>=	(.triggers.cycle_count.limit	//	$th.cycles)
308	then	["cycle_count",	"\(.triggers.cycle_count.current)	changes-required	rounds	(derived	from	the	feedback	history)"]
309	else	null	end	)	as	$trip
310	|	if	$trip	!=	null	and	(.state	//	"CLOSED")	!=	"OPEN"
311	then	.state	=	"OPEN"	|	.history	=	((.history	//	[])	+	[{timestamp:	$ts,	trigger:	$trip[0],	reason:	$trip[1],	source:	"derive"}])
312	else	.state	=	(.state	//	"CLOSED")	end;
313	def	known_ids:	(.derivation.sprint_ids	//	null)	//	((.sprints.list	//	[])	|	map(.id?	//	empty));
314	def	resolve($f;	$now;	$win):
315	.	as	$c
316	|	(if	($c	|	type)	==	"object"	then	$c	else	{}	end)	as	$c
317	|	($c.state	//	$c.status	//	"")	as	$cs
318	|	($c	|	known_ids)	as	$known
319	|	([$f.sprints[]	|	select(.state	!=	"complete")
320	|	"sprint-\(.global_id)"	as	$g	|	.local_label	as	$l
321	|	select(($known	|	index($g))	==	null	and	($l	==	""	or	($known	|	index($l))	==	null))]	|	length	>	0)	as	$new
322	|	((($c.completion	//	{})	|	.merged_sha?	//	"")	|	type	==	"string"	and	length	>	0)	as	$merged
323	|	if	($c.state	//	"")	==	"JACKED_OUT"	or	($c.status	//	"")	==	"JACKED_OUT"	or	$merged	then	"JACKED_OUT"
324	elif	$f.breaker_open	or	$cs	==	"HALTED"	then	"HALTED"
325	elif	$f.all_complete	then	"COMPLETE"
326	elif	$cs	==	"COMPLETE"	and	($new	|	not)	then	"COMPLETE"
327	elif	($c.timestamps.last_activity?	//	null)	|	fresh($now;	$win)	then	"RUNNING"
328	else	"INTERRUPTED"	end;

141	#	atomic_update	FILE	JQ-ARGS...	—	jq	over	FILE	(or	{}	when	FILE	is	absent)	→
142	#	FILE.tmp.$$	→	mv	-f,	under	flock	on	FILE.lock.	Exit	3	on	any	failure;	the
143	#	previous	file	is	untouched.
144	atomic_update()	{
145	local	f="$1";	shift
146	local	tmp="$f.tmp.$$"	rc=0
147	(
148	#	flock	is	util-linux	(Linux);	without	it	(macOS)	the	write	is	still	atomic
149	#	(tmp	+	mv)	but	concurrent	writers	may	interleave	—	last	writer	wins.
150	if	command	-v	flock	>/dev/null	2>&1;	then	flock	-w	5	9	||	{	echo	"run-checkpoint:	lock	timeout	on	$f.lock"	>&2;	exit	3;	};	fi
151	if	[[	-f	"$f"	]];	then
152	jq	"$@"	"$f"	>	"$tmp"	2>/dev/null	||	{	rm	-f	--	"$tmp";	echo	"run-checkpoint:	$f	is	not	valid	JSON	—	not	written"	>&2;	exit	3;	}
153	else
154	jq	"$@"	<<<'{}'	>	"$tmp"	2>/dev/null	||	{	rm	-f	--	"$tmp";	echo	"run-checkpoint:	could	not	build	$f"	>&2;	exit	3;	}
155	fi
156	jq	-e	.	"$tmp"	>/dev/null	2>&1	||	{	rm	-f	--	"$tmp";	echo	"run-checkpoint:	refusing	to	replace	$f	with	unparseable	output"	>&2;	exit	3;	}
157	mv	-f	--	"$tmp"	"$f"
158	)	9>"$f.lock"	||	rc=$?
159	return	$rc
160	}

236	verdict:	($v.verdict	|	if	type	==	"string"	then	.	else	null	end),

# .claude/data/profiles.yaml — `loa.profile` defaults (cycle-129 SDD D-9.1, §3.5;
# DEC-0143, DEC-0152).
#
# One knob, `loa.profile: lean | standard | full` in .loa.config.yaml, sets the
# defaults of the optional surfaces below as a set. Resolution, per key
# (.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh `loa_knob`):
#   1. the key set explicitly in .loa.config.yaml wins;
#   2. else the selected profile's value (unset or unknown profile → standard);
#   3. else the caller's fallback — never reached for a key listed here,
#      because every profile defines every key (tests/unit/profile-lib.bats).
#
# `standard` is the post-cycle-129 example default of each key, written out
# (tests/fixtures/profiles/standard-oracle.json records how each value was
# captured). The two guardrail keys read false here because cycle-129 changed
# their example default (D-4.4, DEC-0161): a migration item, not a profile effect.
#
# No floor key may appear here. The floor config keys are listed once, in
# .claude/data/floor.yaml `floor_keys`; tests/unit/profile-floor.bats fails if a
# profile names one, and profile-lib.sh ignores such a key with a WARN.
# `interview.pacing` is not a profile key: `rounds` is already the default and
# the key would not discriminate between profiles.

  full:

    decisions.surface_at_session_start: true
    karpathy_principles.surgical_diff_warning: true

# .claude/data/floor.yaml — the one tracked floor source (cycle-129 SDD D-9.2, DEC-0166).
#
# The floor is the set of guards, config keys and files no profile, knob or
# cycle task may weaken. Readers:
#   - .claude/scripts/guard-yield.sh and tests/unit/guard-origins.bats: the
#     `floor: true` rows of .claude/data/guard-origins.yaml equal floor_guards.

# deliberately updated in the same change (see the FLOOR_SHA256 constant).
schema_version: 1

floor_guards:
  - fence:FR-1.2b
  - fence:FR-SZ
  - fence:FR-SZ-COPY
  - fence:FR-SZ-DD
  - fence:FR-SZ-EXTRACT
  - fence:FR-SZ-INPLACE
  - fence:FR-SZ-INTERP
  - fence:FR-SZ-LINK
  - fence:FR-SZ-REDIR
  - fence:FR-SZ-TEE
  - fence:FR-SZ2
  - fence:FR-SZ2-COPY
  - fence:FR-SZ2-INPLACE
  - fence:FR-SZ2-REDIR
  - fence:FR-SZ2-RM
  - fence:FR-SZ2-TEE
  - gate:verdict-derive
  - gate:adversarial-review-gate
  - policy:permission-deny-list

floor_keys:

floor_corpus:

    - FR-1.2b
    - "FR-SZ*"

+

The full grammar, both class lists and the default are stated in the block comment above `_bdb_hd_is_interp` in `block-destructive-bash.sh`. In summary:
+
+- **Grammar.** The fence sees literal command text, with CRLF folded to LF. A control character, an unreadable header, more than one heredoc on a header, a non-word or variable delimiter, or a missing terminator makes the whole command scan in full.
+- **Interpreter class.** The body is scanned exactly as before. +

+#!/usr/bin/env bash

+# profile-lib.sh (cycle-129 SDD D-9.1, sprint-256 Task 2.7).
+#
+# Every key under any profile in .claude/data/profiles.yaml must be read
+# through `loa_knob` (.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh), never by a reader's
+# own `yq '.<key> // <default>'`: a direct read skips the profile, and yq's
+# `//` reads an explicit `false` as absent. The check flags a line that names a
+# profile key in yq-path form (a leading dot: `.guardrails.input.enabled`)

+# Optional tables: section_name|heading line. When the section's filter selects
+# no rows, the whole block (the heading, the table header, the marker block and
+# one trailing blank line) is removed from the target instead of rendering an
+# empty table (cycle-129 D-4.5). Restoring rows later needs the heading block
+# back first (`--bootstrap` cannot re-create a heading): insert_generated_section
+# then fails with "Missing markers", naming the section.
+readonly -a OPTIONAL_TABLES=(
+  "agent_teams_constraints|## Agent Teams"
+)
+
 # Flags
 DRY_RUN=false
 VERBOSE=false
@@ -133,6 +144,65 @@ insert_generated_section() {
   fi
 }
 
+# Prints the heading of an optional table section; returns 1 when the section
+# is not optional.
+optional_table_heading() {
+  local section="$1" entry o_name o_heading
+  for entry in "${OPTIONAL_TABLES[@]}"; do
+    IFS='|' read -r o_name o_heading <<< "$entry"
+    if [[ "$o_name" == "$section" ]]; then
+      printf '%s\n' "$o_heading"
+      return 0
+    fi
+  done
+  return 1
+}
+
+# Removes an optional table block from FILE: the exact heading line, the
+# table-header lines between it and the start marker, the marker block, and
+# one blank line after the end marker. A file without the start marker is
+# already pruned (no-op). Anything else between the heading and the start
+# marker, a missing heading or a missing end marker is an error and leaves
+# FILE untouched.
+prune_optional_table() {
+  local file="$1" section="$2" heading="$3"
+  if ! grep -q "@constraint-generated: start ${section} " "$file"; then
+    verbose "Optional section ${section} already absent from ${file}"
+    return 0
+  fi
+  local tmp="${file}.prune-tmp" rc=0
+  awk -v heading="$heading" \
+      -v start="@constraint-generated: start ${section} " \
+      -v end="@constraint-generated: end ${section} " '
+    function flush(   i) { for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) print buf[i]; n = 0 }
+    state == "" && $0 == heading { state = "head"; n = 0; buf[++n] = $0; next }
+    state == "head" {
+      if (index($0, start)) { state = "skip"; n = 0; next }
+      if ($0 ~ /^\|/ || $0 ~ /^[[:space:]]*$/) { buf[++n] = $0; next }
+      flush(); state = ""; print; next
+    }
+    state == "skip" { if (index($0, end)) state = "after"; next }
+    state == "after" { state = "done"; if ($0 ~ /^[[:space:]]*$/) next }
+    { print }
+    END {
+      if (state == "head") flush()
+      if (state == "skip") exit 3
+      if (state == "" ) exit 4
+    }
+  ' "$file" > "$tmp" || rc=$?
+  if [[ "$rc" -ne 0 ]]; then
+    rm -f "$tmp"
+    case "$rc" in
+      3) log "ERROR: ${file}: no end marker for optional section '${section}'" ;;
+      4) log "ERROR: ${file}: optional section '${section}' has markers but no '${heading}' heading directly above its table" ;;
+      *) log "ERROR: ${file}: pruning optional section '${section}' failed (awk exit ${rc})" ;;
+    esac
+    return 1
+  fi
+  mv "$tmp" "$file"
+  verbose "Pruned empty optional section ${section} (${heading}) from ${file}"
+}
+
 # ============================================================================
 # Bootstrap: insert markers into target files
 # ============================================================================
@@ -299,6 +369,19 @@ generate_all_sections() {

       IFS='|' read -r s_target s_template s_filter <<< "$s_data"
